claims.statement: Gross margin on a web ad impression at the seller in 2000 — Yahoo's audited figure was 86.5% and fell to 78.1% in 2001. The number that matters is the contrast: gross margins were print-beating while operating results were catastrophic, because selling an impression cost far more than serving it. Yahoo spent 38% of 2000 revenue on sales and marketing and still lost $92.8M in 2001; ad networks made only 25-40% gross margin because they paid the publisher out of the same impression.
claims.unit: percent gross margin per impression
claims.method: Anchored on Yahoo's audited FY2000 accounts: net revenues $1,110.178M less cost of revenues $149.744M = 86.5% gross margin (78.1% in 2001 on $717.422M and $157.001M). Cross-checked bottom-up against the unit figures above: (0.0070 - 0.0009) / 0.0070 = 87%. Central set slightly below Yahoo at 85% because the market-wide mix includes ad networks, whose gross margin was 25.3% in 2000 (32.6% excluding a one-off write-off) since publisher payouts sit in their cost of revenue. CI lower bound of 70% reflects that network-intermediated share.

claims.statement: Local and retail buyers account for about 23.5 percent of US advertising spend in 2025, roughly $93.5B. claims.method: SOURCED BY: NOT SOURCED AS A MONEY TYPE, which is why the grade falls from B to C. The source that carried the B grade - BIA's $169B US local advertising total - measures a different object: BIA's own published definition is all media selling access to LOCAL AUDIENCES to ALL advertiser types INCLUDING national and regional companies. That is geography of inventory, not class of buyer. What IS available, and is the hunt's largest free evidence upgrade, is BIA's own advertiser-type ratio, published in summary form at $116.4B regional-and-national marketers against $59.2B SMBs (SMB = 33.7 percent), corroborated by the independent BIA/Kelsey 2015 vintage at SMB $50.4B of a $140.7B local total (35.9 percent). That ratio grades B, but the derived 2025 pool needs a regional-tier allocation and a rail conversion on top of it, so the pool is C. RAIL: MAGNA media-owner advertising revenue, $398B for 2025 (digital pure players $294B + traditional media owners $104B, which sums exactly, so DIRECT MAIL IS OUT of this rail). All four pools are defined ex-direct-mail to match, which is the fix for the mechanical residual depression the era-7 verifier flagged: the superseded residual was computed with direct mail excluded from the denominator but present in two subtracted pools. RAIL SENSITIVITY EXCEEDS EVERY INTERVAL IN THIS SPLIT: IRS SOI corporate advertising deductions read $473,153m for 2022 against MAGNA's $325,000m, a $148B wedge that is overwhelmingly direct-response and retail money. Any chart of this split must name its rail in the axis label, not the footnote. || AGGREGATION: median of three lens centrals (structural-proxy 19.6, reference-class 23.5, decomposition 23.9). No extremizing. This is the best-supported of the four pools methodologically - three genuinely independent routes, each run by all three lenses. || ROUTE L-A, BIA's own advertiser-type cut, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.40 (0.42 / 0.40 / 0.35). PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENT, and it is the decisive one: BIA's population is buyers-of-local-inventory, which includes national and regional companies, so the correction on the record is DOWN and large. SMB-share drift is measured rather than assumed, 35.9 percent (2015) to 33.7 percent (current), a 2.2pp decline over a decade. Local direct mail (about $3-3.8B on BIA's own stated 90/10 national/local rule) is removed to match the ex-direct-mail denominator, and the classified and vertical money BIA admits sits inside its PC/Laptop digital definition (about $2-3.5B) is reassigned to classified so the two pools are disjoint. THE OPEN JUDGEMENT: BIA lumps 'regional' with 'national', and the regional tier is local-retail money in the Coen/NAA sense; the lenses allocate 30, 40 and about 44 percent of that lump to local retail. At 0 percent the pool reads 14.3 percent, at 45 percent it reads 24.1 percent. This one parameter is the widest unverified step in era 7. NOTE: the two BIA vintages are ONE compiler, so L-A is one route across all three lenses. || ROUTE L-B, medium-by-medium buyer-side build from government and trade rails plus platform filings, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.38 (0.38 / 0.00 bound-only / 0.40). PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: TIME GAP - the Census SAS national/local split stops at reference year 2010 and RAB thins after 2021, so both are carried forward 4 to 15 years; radio's local share is stable across two independent readings five years apart (72.2 percent Census 2010, 74.1 percent RAB 2015), which bounds the drift small for that medium, while TV's assumed-flat 36-40 percent is the weakest link. SELLER-SIDE VERSUS BUYER-SIDE - the Census classifies who bought the time, not what the money was for, which correctly leaves national direct-response TV out of local. The platform local-bought shares (Meta about 32 percent of US, Google about 20 percent) are calibrated judgements, not measurements, and swing the route by about $15B. || ROUTE L-C, establishment count times category advertising intensity, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.20 (0.20 / 0.20 / 0.25). PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: SMB survey average revenue per advertiser captures websites, SEO, promotions and marketing services that sit OUTSIDE the media rail, direction down about 20 percent; the count-based approach misses local advertisers who buy only traditional media and never touch a self-serve platform, direction up about 10 percent; and SMB is not the same as local - a $2m-revenue direct-to-consumer brand buying nationally on Meta is national direct response. NEAR-DUPLICATES DECLARED: the three lenses' parameterisations differ (3.5m x $22k; 4.5m x $14k; 4.0m x about $24k) but are one route, and they converge on $62B, $63B and $63B for the SMB leg. || INTERVAL: min lower to max upper across the lenses. Its width is definitional, not statistical: the regional-tier allocation alone spans it.

claims.statement: Classified buyers - individuals and businesses paying to list a job, a car, a home or an item - account for about 2.5 percent of US advertising spend in 2025, roughly $9.95B, essentially all of it placed with digital marketplaces and job boards. On a listings-inclusive reading the money type is nearer $21B, of which $12-16B sits outside every published advertising series.
claims.unit: percent of US advertising spend, 2025 (MAGNA media-owner rail, $398B, direct mail excluded)
claims.method: SOURCED BY: SOURCED FOR 2008-2021 AT GRADE A ON THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS - the hunt's main finding, which overturns the note that no modern source publishes this. (1) US Census Bureau Service Annual Survey, NAICS 511110, 'Breakdown of Revenue by Advertising Type: classified advertising', free, 2005-2021 with 2012 and 2022 suppressed: $8,087m (2008) falling to $1,978m (2021), a government probability survey independent of NAA, Coen, IAB, MAGNA and BIA. (2) The same survey's NAICS 511140 directory advertising space line, free, 2005-2020: $11,400m (2008) to $1,781m (2020), replacing the two trade blogs the record previously cited. (3) IAB/PwC's classifieds format line, free, with its own share to about 2016 and a stated dollar figure inside 'Other' to 2021, $3.2B (2008) to $5.3B (2021). Overlap test passes: NAA $5,030m against Census $4,840m for newspaper classified in 2011, a 3.9 percent gap. The 2008 anchor is fully grade A at $22.7B. NOT SOURCED: reference years 2022-2026 on any leg, and the marketplace and listings leg in every year. THE 2025 ANCHOR THEREFORE STAYS GRADE C: every sourced leg stops at reference year 2021 and nothing free reaches the anchor year. RAIL: MAGNA media-owner advertising revenue, $398B for 2025 (digital pure players $294B + traditional media owners $104B, which sums exactly, so DIRECT MAIL IS OUT of this rail). All four pools are defined ex-direct-mail to match, which is the fix for the mechanical residual depression the era-7 verifier flagged: the superseded residual was computed with direct mail excluded from the denominator but present in two subtracted pools. RAIL SENSITIVITY EXCEEDS EVERY INTERVAL IN THIS SPLIT: IRS SOI corporate advertising deductions read $473,153m for 2022 against MAGNA's $325,000m, a $148B wedge that is overwhelmingly direct-response and retail money. Any chart of this split must name its rail in the axis label, not the footnote. || AGGREGATION: median of three lens centrals (structural-proxy 1.9, reference-class 3.4, decomposition 2.5). No extremizing. Three routes, each run by all three lenses. || ROUTE C-A, decomposition of IAB's 'Other' bucket ($12.5B in FY2025) using its own last-published internal composition, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.45. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: BUCKET COMPOSITION BREAK - digital audio left 'Other' after FY2021 and directories were named into it from FY2022, so the FY2021 shares cannot be applied to the FY2025 total directly and the raw series must never be read across that join. TIME DRIFT - lead generation grew with the performance market while classified listing revenue migrated to transaction fees, so classifieds' share of the classified-plus-lead-generation pair falls; the lenses set it at 45, 55 and about 64 percent, and that single parameter is where the lens spread lives. || ROUTE C-B, Census SAS print legs extrapolated past their discontinuation, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.30. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENT: extrapolation across four to five unpublished reference years at each leg's own observed compound rate (newspaper classified -10 to -11 percent a year, directories -13.6 to -15 percent a year), with the print-only portion of the directory line separated from the digital portion already counted in C-A. The route's INPUTS are grade A to 2021; only the carry-forward is C. || ROUTE C-C, marketplace and listings leg rebuilt bottom-up from EDGAR and company disclosure, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.25. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: LISTED-COMPANY BIAS - EDGAR filers over-represent consolidated national portals and miss private and regional portals, direction up 8 to 15 percent; DEFINITIONAL BIAS the other way - Zillow Premier Agent, Angi and LinkedIn Recruiter seats are arguably lead generation or service fees rather than listing advertisements, direction down 10 to 15 percent; the two roughly cancel, so the central is not shifted and the interval is widened instead. De-duplicated against C-A, because roughly $3.5-7B of the listings revenue is already inside IAB's 'Other'. || INTERVAL: min lower to max upper across the lenses. WARNING, and it is a scope statement rather than an uncertainty band: above about 2.8 percent of the market (about $11.1B) the interval is FRAME, not measurement error, because two lenses set their upper bound on a widened denominator that counts the listings successors ($410-421B rather than $398B). The in-frame-only interval is 1.4 to 2.8 percent, i.e. $5.6B to $11.1B. The two readings are both correct on their own frames and must never be blended in a chart. || SCOPE ALTERNATIVE, recorded because it is the era's boundary-shift argument in one number: on a listings-inclusive reading the classified money type is about $21B (range $15-29B), of which roughly $12-16B sits outside every published US advertising total. Indeed's US revenue alone ($5.31B) approaches the whole of IAB's $12.5B 'Other' bucket. || DEFINITIONAL FORK 1: lead generation is roughly $4.5-6B of IAB's 'Other'. Two lenses move it to direct response on the ground that money paid per acquired lead is action-priced; one keeps a portion at weight 0.35 on the ground that a firm paying per lead for a roofer is buying what the classified page sold. That call produces almost the whole 1.9-to-3.4 spread. DEFINITIONAL FORK 2: directory money is carried in classified here, following the record, the hunt and IAB's own bucket; the alternative moves this pool from 2.5 to about 2.2 percent in 2025 but from 9.3 to about 5.2 percent in 2008.

claims.method: SOURCED BY: POOL NOT SOURCED; ONE INPUT SOURCED AT GRADE A. IAB/PwC's 'Revenues by pricing model' exhibit publishes the performance-priced share of US digital annually 2004-2019 - 57 percent for 2008, 62-66 percent across 2010-2019, 62.1 percent at HY2019 - which converts 'two-thirds of digital is performance-priced' from an assumption into a published number for twelve of the nineteen era years. The exhibit was discontinued after HY2019, so 2020-2026 is EXTRAPOLATION. The only source that ever sized the whole pool, DMA/IHS Global Insight ($153.3B in 2010, 54.2 percent of US ad expenditure), died inside the era. Pool grade C. RAIL: MAGNA media-owner advertising revenue, $398B for 2025 (digital pure players $294B + traditional media owners $104B, which sums exactly, so DIRECT MAIL IS OUT of this rail). All four pools are defined ex-direct-mail to match, which is the fix for the mechanical residual depression the era-7 verifier flagged: the superseded residual was computed with direct mail excluded from the denominator but present in two subtracted pools. RAIL SENSITIVITY EXCEEDS EVERY INTERVAL IN THIS SPLIT: IRS SOI corporate advertising deductions read $473,153m for 2022 against MAGNA's $325,000m, a $148B wedge that is overwhelmingly direct-response and retail money. Any chart of this split must name its rail in the axis label, not the footnote. || AGGREGATION: median of three lens centrals (structural-proxy 38.0, reference-class 36.5, decomposition 40.7). No extremizing. THE APPARENT AGREEMENT IS AN ARTEFACT: all three centrals are three parameterisations of ONE unobserved quantity, the performance-priced share of US digital in 2025, which the lenses set at 60.0, 62.6 and 67.7 percent. Their 4.2pp dispersion measures disagreement about one parameter, not independent convergence, which is why the interval is taken from the combined lens bounds and not from the dispersion. || ROUTE D-A, performance-priced share applied to IAB's mutually exclusive FY2025 format partition, then strip local-bought digital and add national traditional direct response, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.50. All three lenses run this route, and one lens's two variants (mix-shift decomposition of the 2019-2025 increment versus direct format weighting) are near-duplicates of each other because both consume the same IAB partition and the same HY2019 anchor - that is one route, not two. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: pricing basis is not buyer intent, with offsetting errors in both directions netting small; local-bought digital is removed so the pools stay disjoint; and the load-bearing step is extrapolating IAB's published 62.1 percent across the five unmeasured years that contain Performance Max, Advantage+ and the rise of retail media. || ROUTE D-B, the DMA/IHS direct-marketing pool decayed forward and rail-converted, WEIGHT 0.45 in the lens that ran it. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: DMA's denominator sits on a billings and deductions rail rather than a media-owner rail, and is converted at IRS SOI / MAGNA 2022 = 1.456; DMA's pool includes local direct marketing and lead generation, so the national portion is taken at 65 percent; the 2010 share of 54.2 percent is carried UP to about 62 percent for search, retail media and performance social growth. This route shares no input with D-A - different compiler, different decade, different rail - and lands at 37.6 percent against D-A's 38.5 percent. THE ONE GENUINELY INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE IN THE ERA. || ROUTE D-C, advertiser-stated performance share (WARC/Ebiquity), WEIGHT 0.00 to 0.20, bound only. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: global to US, +2 to +4pp; large-advertiser panel to whole market, +5 to +10pp; the survey conflates 'performance' as short-term activation intent with 'direct response' as measurable-action pricing. Adjusted it reads 44 to 57 percent and sets the top of the interval. || NEAR-DUPLICATE DECLARED AND DISCOUNTED: the seller-filings route (Alphabet, Meta and Amazon 10-Ks) is not independent of D-A, because Amazon's sponsored-product revenue sits inside IAB's search line, so it re-counts what D-A counts once. || RETIRED: the superseded path (b) - search plus commerce media plus 70 percent of social - is not a route. It sums $260B of a $294.6B market before any subtraction, because IAB's format partition already exhausts the total and commerce media and social are cross-cuts on top of it. All three lenses retired it independently. || INTERVAL: min lower to max upper across the lenses. It is deliberately NOT drawn from the 4.2pp lens dispersion, which is spuriously tight.

What IS available, and is the hunt's largest free evidence upgrade, is BIA's own advertiser-type ratio, published in summary form at $116.4B regional-and-national marketers against $59.2B SMBs (SMB = 33.7 percent), corroborated by the independent BIA/Kelsey 2015 vintage at SMB $50.4B of a $140.7B local total (35.9 percent). RAIL: MAGNA media-owner advertising revenue, $398B for 2025 (digital pure players $294B + traditional media owners $104B, which sums exactly, so DIRECT MAIL IS OUT of this rail). All four pools are defined ex-direct-mail to match, which is the fix for the mechanical residual depression the era-7 verifier flagged: the superseded residual was computed with direct mail excluded from the denominator but present in two subtracted pools. RAIL SENSITIVITY EXCEEDS EVERY INTERVAL IN THIS SPLIT: IRS SOI corporate advertising deductions read $473,153m for 2022 against MAGNA's $325,000m, a $148B wedge that is overwhelmingly direct-response and retail money. No extremizing. This is the best-supported of the four pools methodologically - three genuinely independent routes, each run by all three lenses. || ROUTE L-A, BIA's own advertiser-type cut, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.40 (0.42 / 0.40 / 0.35). PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENT, and it is the decisive one: BIA's population is buyers-of-local-inventory, which includes national and regional companies, so the correction on the record is DOWN and large. SMB-share drift is measured rather than assumed, 35.9 percent (2015) to 33.7 percent (current), a 2.2pp decline over a decade. Local direct mail (about $3-3.8B on BIA's own stated 90/10 national/local rule) is removed to match the ex-direct-mail denominator, and the classified and vertical money BIA admits sits inside its PC/Laptop digital definition (about $2-3.5B) is reassigned to classified so the two pools are disjoint. THE OPEN JUDGEMENT: BIA lumps 'regional' with 'national', and the regional tier is local-retail money in the Coen/NAA sense; the lenses allocate 30, 40 and about 44 percent of that lump to local retail. At 0 percent the pool reads 14.3 percent, at 45 percent it reads 24.1 percent. This one parameter is the widest unverified step in era 7. NOTE: the two BIA vintages are ONE compiler, so L-A is one route across all three lenses. || ROUTE L-B, medium-by-medium buyer-side build from government and trade rails plus platform filings, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.38 (0.38 / 0.00 bound-only / 0.40). PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: TIME GAP - the Census SAS national/local split stops at reference year 2010 and RAB thins after 2021, so both are carried forward 4 to 15 years; radio's local share is stable across two independent readings five years apart (72.2 percent Census 2010, 74.1 percent RAB 2015), which bounds the drift small for that medium, while TV's assumed-flat 36-40 percent is the weakest link. SELLER-SIDE VERSUS BUYER-SIDE - the Census classifies who bought the time, not what the money was for, which correctly leaves national direct-response TV out of local. The platform local-bought shares (Meta about 32 percent of US, Google about 20 percent) are calibrated judgements, not measurements, and swing the route by about $15B. || ROUTE L-C, establishment count times category advertising intensity, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.20 (0.20 / 0.20 / 0.25). PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: SMB survey average revenue per advertiser captures websites, SEO, promotions and marketing services that sit OUTSIDE the media rail, direction down about 20 percent; the count-based approach misses local advertisers who buy only traditional media and never touch a self-serve platform, direction up about 10 percent; and SMB is not the same as local - a $2m-revenue direct-to-consumer brand buying nationally on Meta is national direct response. NEAR-DUPLICATES DECLARED: the three lenses' parameterisations differ (3.5m x $22k; 4.5m x $14k; 4.0m x about $24k) but are one route, and they converge on $62B, $63B and $63B for the SMB leg. || INTERVAL: min lower to max upper across the lenses. (3) IAB/PwC's classifieds format line, free, with its own share to about 2016 and a stated dollar figure inside 'Other' to 2021, $3.2B (2008) to $5.3B (2021). Overlap test passes: NAA $5,030m against Census $4,840m for newspaper classified in 2011, a 3.9 percent gap. The 2008 anchor is fully grade A at $22.7B. NOT SOURCED: reference years 2022-2026 on any leg, and the marketplace and listings leg in every year. THE 2025 ANCHOR THEREFORE STAYS GRADE C: every sourced leg stops at reference year 2021 and nothing free reaches the anchor year. RAIL: MAGNA media-owner advertising revenue, $398B for 2025 (digital pure players $294B + traditional media owners $104B, which sums exactly, so DIRECT MAIL IS OUT of this rail). RAIL SENSITIVITY EXCEEDS EVERY INTERVAL IN THIS SPLIT: IRS SOI corporate advertising deductions read $473,153m for 2022 against MAGNA's $325,000m, a $148B wedge that is overwhelmingly direct-response and retail money. Any chart of this split must name its rail in the axis label, not the footnote. || AGGREGATION: median of three lens centrals (structural-proxy 1.9, reference-class 3.4, decomposition 2.5). No extremizing. Three routes, each run by all three lenses. || ROUTE C-A, decomposition of IAB's 'Other' bucket ($12.5B in FY2025) using its own last-published internal composition, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.45. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: BUCKET COMPOSITION BREAK - digital audio left 'Other' after FY2021 and directories were named into it from FY2022, so the FY2021 shares cannot be applied to the FY2025 total directly and the raw series must never be read across that join. TIME DRIFT - lead generation grew with the performance market while classified listing revenue migrated to transaction fees, so classifieds' share of the classified-plus-lead-generation pair falls; the lenses set it at 45, 55 and about 64 percent, and that single parameter is where the lens spread lives. || ROUTE C-B, Census SAS print legs extrapolated past their discontinuation, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.30. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENT: extrapolation across four to five unpublished reference years at each leg's own observed compound rate (newspaper classified -10 to -11 percent a year, directories -13.6 to -15 percent a year), with the print-only portion of the directory line separated from the digital portion already counted in C-A. The route's INPUTS are grade A to 2021; only the carry-forward is C. || ROUTE C-C, marketplace and listings leg rebuilt bottom-up from EDGAR and company disclosure, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.25. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: LISTED-COMPANY BIAS - EDGAR filers over-represent consolidated national portals and miss private and regional portals, direction up 8 to 15 percent; DEFINITIONAL BIAS the other way - Zillow Premier Agent, Angi and LinkedIn Recruiter seats are arguably lead generation or service fees rather than listing advertisements, direction down 10 to 15 percent; the two roughly cancel, so the central is not shifted and the interval is widened instead. De-duplicated against C-A, because roughly $3.5-7B of the listings revenue is already inside IAB's 'Other'. || INTERVAL: min lower to max upper across the lenses. WARNING, and it is a scope statement rather than an uncertainty band: above about 2.8 percent of the market (about $11.1B) the interval is FRAME, not measurement error, because two lenses set their upper bound on a widened denominator that counts the listings successors ($410-421B rather than $398B). The in-frame-only interval is 1.4 to 2.8 percent, i.e. $5.6B to $11.1B. The two readings are both correct on their own frames and must never be blended in a chart. || SCOPE ALTERNATIVE, recorded because it is the era's boundary-shift argument in one number: on a listings-inclusive reading the classified money type is about $21B (range $15-29B), of which roughly $12-16B sits outside every published US advertising total. Indeed's US revenue alone ($5.31B) approaches the whole of IAB's $12.5B 'Other' bucket. || DEFINITIONAL FORK 1: lead generation is roughly $4.5-6B of IAB's 'Other'. Two lenses move it to direct response on the ground that money paid per acquired lead is action-priced; one keeps a portion at weight 0.35 on the ground that a firm paying per lead for a roofer is buying what the classified page sold. That call produces almost the whole 1.9-to-3.4 spread. DEFINITIONAL FORK 2: directory money is carried in classified here, following the record, the hunt and IAB's own bucket; the alternative moves this pool from 2.5 to about 2.2 percent in 2025 but from 9.3 to about 5.2 percent in 2008.

No extremizing. THE APPARENT AGREEMENT IS AN ARTEFACT: all three centrals are three parameterisations of ONE unobserved quantity, the performance-priced share of US digital in 2025, which the lenses set at 60.0, 62.6 and 67.7 percent. Their 4.2pp dispersion measures disagreement about one parameter, not independent convergence, which is why the interval is taken from the combined lens bounds and not from the dispersion. || ROUTE D-A, performance-priced share applied to IAB's mutually exclusive FY2025 format partition, then strip local-bought digital and add national traditional direct response, MEDIAN WEIGHT 0.50. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: pricing basis is not buyer intent, with offsetting errors in both directions netting small; local-bought digital is removed so the pools stay disjoint; and the load-bearing step is extrapolating IAB's published 62.1 percent across the five unmeasured years that contain Performance Max, Advantage+ and the rise of retail media. || ROUTE D-B, the DMA/IHS direct-marketing pool decayed forward and rail-converted, WEIGHT 0.45 in the lens that ran it. PROXY-POPULATION-GAP ADJUSTMENTS: DMA's denominator sits on a billings and deductions rail rather than a media-owner rail, and is converted at IRS SOI / MAGNA 2022 = 1.456; DMA's pool includes local direct marketing and lead generation, so the national portion is taken at 65 percent; the 2010 share of 54.2 percent is carried UP to about 62 percent for search, retail media and performance social growth. This route shares no input with D-A - different compiler, different decade, different rail - and lands at 37.6 percent against D-A's 38.5 percent. claims.statement: The four reconciled money-type pools sum to 100.6 percent of the $398B observed US total for 2025, over-allocating it by about $2.4 billion. claims.unit: percentage points of the $398B observed 2025 US total; negative means the four pools over-allocate
claims.method: The four medians sum to 100.6 percent of the $398B observed total, or $400.4B, so the residual is NEGATIVE: the pools over-allocate by $2.4B, they do not fall short. THE CAUSE IS THE AGGREGATION, NOT THE EVIDENCE. National brand and direct response are constructed complements - in every lens one is computed as, or against, the residual left by the other. Taking the median of each pool independently picks national brand from the reference-class lens (36.6) and direct response from the structural-proxy lens (38.0), a combination no lens produced and one that breaks the complementarity each lens enforced internally. Each lens's own partition closes at 99.2, 100.0 and 100.0 percent; only the median-of-medians overshoots. It is reported rather than absorbed, because forcing closure by shaving national brand would hide the one place where the lenses genuinely conflict. || SENSITIVITY, stated so the number is attackable: the reference-class lens built its shares on a $405B rail (the MAGNA/EMARKETER blend the era record carries at e7-scale-001), which sits inside the observation's own interval. Rebasing its dollar figures onto the observed $398B and re-taking the medians gives 101.56 percent, a residual of -1.6pp or -$6.2B; that is the interval's lower end. The upper end is 0.0pp, reached if classified is taken at the structural-proxy lens's in-frame 1.9 percent and national brand at the decomposition lens's 32.9 percent. || SEPARATELY, AND NOT PART OF THIS RESIDUAL, two quantities sit outside the frame on both sides of the ledger and are excluded from numerator and denominator alike: roughly $38B of US direct mail (Winterberry $37.3B for 2024) and roughly $12-16B of classified-successor listing revenue. Interval spans a 2.2-4.0T denominator. The distribution comparison uses FY2025 TAC of $59,926M at a 20.3% rate; applying that rate to Search & other revenue gives about $45B, divided by 5.0-5.6T queries = $0.008-0.009.

claims.method: Arithmetic on two filed series: 1 - AdSense TAC / Google Network advertising revenue. 2006: 1 - 3134.6/4159.831 = 24.65%. 2007: 1 - 4543.0/5787.938 = 21.51%. 2008: 1 - 5284.3/6714.688 = 21.30%. claims.statement: Within owned-site growth 2002-2007 (34.6x), a log decomposition attributes 52-56% to query volume and 44-48% to revenue per query. The two paths differ only in the query denominator: 65.7bn to 483bn queries with yield rising from $0.0047 to $0.022 gives 56.3% volume, and 65.7bn to 415bn with yield rising to $0.0256 gives 52.0%.
claims.unit: % of Google owned-site revenue growth 2002-2007 attributable to query volume rather than yield (log decomposition)
claims.method: Owned-site revenue multiple 10624.705/306.978 = 34.611, ln = 3.5442. Query and yield estimates are taken from the era-6 record's own grade-C claims e6-pricing-008 and e6-unit_econ-001, which were built from Google's disclosed query statements and comScore's 2007 measurement. Volume share = ln(volume multiple)/ln(revenue multiple). High-volume path: ln(7.3516)/3.5442 = 0.5629. Low-volume path: ln(6.3166)/3.5442 = 0.5201. Central is the midpoint. The whole decomposition inherits the grade-C denominators; the interval reflects denominator uncertainty only, not the possibility that Google's query mix changed.
